title: How far Henderson's band travelled; tenure of two and a half years
summary: Fletcher never went west of Chicago or south of Oklahoma City; once the band toured without him under his wife's management. Procope stayed about two and a half years.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did you travel with Fletcher? You must have. That picture on the boardwalk --

Yes, I travelled. But Fletcher, his traveling wasn't as extensive as let's say as Duke's was later on, Duke Ellington's band later on. You know, Fletcher never went further west than Chicago, and he never got further south than Oklahoma City. That was the extent of his traveling. Of course New England. But he never went to the deep South or whatever.
Not with a band. He did go, I think, earlier, with Ethel Waters, when he was with Black Swan.
Oh, I suppose, I suppose he did, yes. But I mean while I was with him with the band, no. There was one trip the band made without Fletcher, and Fletcher's wife was in charge of the band at that time.
No, she was just sort of managing the band. I think Rex Stewart was --

I never knew why that was. I think Fletcher had something else to do where he -- I suppose money was concerned, with the booking agents, or whatever. Or maybe he was making appearances somewhere or something like that.
But you were with Fletcher for almost three years, or three years? Way up till 1934?
About two and a half years, I believe, yeah.
Was that an uninterrupted two and a half years?
Oh, yes. Oh, yes, yes. Fletcher, he -- he worked steady. He worked steady and got bookings. He got bookings, you know. But again, I say then suddenly --
Can you hold it a minute?
